    Variation partitioning between environment and space

    geo_varpart.Rd

    Separates the variation in species composition explained by measured environmental variables from that explained by spatial structure, as in the spatial variation partitioning of CANOCO and Borcard et al. (2018):

    1. Spatial predictors are distance-based Moran's eigenvector maps (geo_mem()) of the site coordinates.

    2. MEMs are kept only if they explain composition significantly as a set, and then chosen by forward selection with the double stopping criterion (Blanchet et al. 2008), so space is not over-fitted.

    3. The variation is partitioned (vegan::varpart()) into the fraction explained by environment alone [a], shared by environment and space [b], explained by space alone [c], and unexplained, each as an adjusted \(R^2\). The fractions that can be tested ([a], [c] and the two sets) are tested by permutation in partial redundancy analyses.

    Read [a] as the effect of the measured environment free of spatial structure; [c] as spatial structure not explained by the measured environment (unmeasured variables, dispersal or biotic processes); [b] as spatially structured environment, which cannot be attributed to either alone. Shared fractions are not tested and can be negative when the two sets suppress each other.

    Usage

    geo_varpart(
  data,
  site = site,
  species = species,
  abundance = NULL,
  env,
  env_vars,
  lon = "lon",
  lat = "lat",
  method = c("euclidean", "haversine"),
  transform = "hellinger",
  alpha = 0.05,
  permutations = 999
)

    Arguments

    data

    Long community data: one row per site and species.

    site, species, abundance

    Columns of data.

    env

    A data frame with one row per site: the site column, the coordinates and the environmental variables.

    env_vars

    Names of the environmental variables in env.

    lon, lat

    Names of the coordinate columns in env.

    method

    Distance for the MEMs: "euclidean" for projected or local coordinates, "haversine" for longitude and latitude.

    transform

    Transformation of the community matrix (vegan::decostand() method); "hellinger" by default.

    alpha

    Significance level for keeping and selecting MEMs.

    permutations

    Number of permutations.

    Value

    A list of class tmr_geo_varpart: fractions (a tibble of fraction, meaning, adjusted R2, statistic and p-value), mems (the selected MEMs) and fit (the varpart object).

    References

    Blanchet, F. G., Legendre, P. and Borcard, D. (2008). Forward selection of explanatory variables. Ecology, 89, 2623-2632. doi:10.1890/07-0986.1

    Borcard, D., Gillet, F. and Legendre, P. (2018). Numerical Ecology with R, second edition. Springer. Chapter 7.

    Peres-Neto, P. R., Legendre, P., Dray, S. and Borcard, D. (2006). Variation partitioning of species data matrices: estimation and comparison of fractions. Ecology, 87, 2614-2625.

    Examples

    data("mite", "mite.env", "mite.xy", package = "vegan")
long <- data.frame(
  site = rep(rownames(mite), ncol(mite)),
  species = rep(colnames(mite), each = nrow(mite)),
  n = unlist(mite)
)
env <- cbind(site = rownames(mite), mite.xy, mite.env)
geo_varpart(long, abundance = n, env = env,
  env_vars = c("SubsDens", "WatrCont"), lon = "x", lat = "y",
  permutations = 199)
#> Variation partitioning: environment and space
#> 10 MEMs selected: MEM2, MEM3, MEM8, MEM1, MEM6, MEM4, MEM9, MEM16, MEM7, and
#> MEM20
#> # A tibble: 6 × 5
#>   fraction             meaning                          adj_r2 statistic p.value
#>   <chr>                <chr>                             <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1 [a+b] environment    all variation the measured envi… 0.307      16.3    0.005
#> 2 [b+c] space          all variation the selected MEMs… 0.442       6.46   0.005
#> 3 [a] environment only environment free of spatial str… 0.0590      4.49   0.005
#> 4 [b] shared           spatially structured environmen… 0.194      NA     NA    
#> 5 [c] space only       spatial structure not explained… 0.248       3.61   0.005
#> 6 [d] unexplained      residual variation               0.499      NA     NA
